pr_title: Add automated Blazor WebView test using Photino
pr_body:
I'm adding a 'testMode' to the PhotinoTestApp that automatically executes some tests. Well, just _one_ test: load Blazor in a WebView (using Photino), click a button, and verify some text was updated.

Next steps:
* ~Figure out how to automate it to run on checkin/CI/dev tests. I'm not sure if we have any tests that pop up Windows UI~
* ~Clean up the code (it's super hacky, but it does work)~

Fixes #50193
pr_comments:
Looks like this PR hasn't been active for some time and the codebase could have been changed in the meantime.
To make sure no conflicting changes have occurred, please rerun validation before merging. You can do this by leaving an `/azp run` comment here (requires commit rights), or by simply closing and reopening.

Photino is nice. It's gives you this kind of "just build exe and run" option which Maui with it's hard dependent windows special magical store app doesn't.

Also, it's possible to use Photino to run some Linux tests too, but I'm not sure whether that's a priority at all.
This is what it looks like when it passes locally: And this is an example of a failure mode when I make the test fail on purpose:

Alright this is the state of things:
* The test runs locally fine on Windows
* The test runs on CI (Helix) fine on Windows
* The test is skipped on Ubuntu and macOS because it doesn't work there right now (plenty of comments in the code explaining what I found)
* The test correctly failed when I revert the RC1 fix that addressed the Preview 7 break: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/49958 (this is the bug the originally motivated having more tests run earlier, and having this new test would have found the bug)
* The test produces a ton of log output (~400 lines or so) that is super helpful in debugging why the test doesn't work, and I'd like to keep that (it's totally harmless in successful runs, and very useful in case of failure)

So I think it's ready to review.

Pinging @MackinnonBuck in particular, but all of @dotnet/aspnet-blazor-eng is graciously encouraged to participate.
@SteveSandersonMS - I think I've applied all your feedback so I'd appreciate another once-over. I also added even more code comments because this test pattern is... unusual.
Alright, tests are green and passing on CI, and I believe all PR review comments are addressed.
Oh, it's auto-merged. I didn't mean to trigger that. Up to you whether you want to follow up on the final comments here.

Also, this is merged into `main` which is now .NET 9. There's definitely value in backporting it to .NET 8 too, since that's an LTS release and we don't ever want to break WebView in servicing.

I'm going to see if the bot can auto-backport it, but if not, would you be open to making that happen?

issue_context.title: Add automated Blazor Hybrid test
issue_context.body: We need to come up with at least a basic test to verify that Blazor Hybrid is working when we make changes to various parts of Blazor. Currently the only way we find out is via vendor manual testing, and when we eventually consume the aspnetcore bits in the dotnet/maui repo. We need a much faster way to find out if we are regressing critical behavior.

review_comments:
At `$(SharedSourceRoot)\CommandLineUtils\Utilities\DotNetMuxer.cs`, we have a utility that figures out the name and full path of the .NET "muxer" (i.e., CLI executable), which we use in other tests.

I honestly have no idea what advantages that offers versus just hardcoding the string `"dotnet"` like you have done here, so have no specific opinion that you should change to using `DotNetMuxer`. But if you want to be maximally consistent with other test code, that API exists.

It might be due to the ASP.NET Core repo being configured to emit `bin`/`obj` build output to `$(RepoRoot)/artifacts/...` instead of into a subdir within each project.

In `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.E2ETests.csproj`, we explicitly reset the `BaseOutputPath` and `OutputPath` MSBuild properties to override that and get the default `bin`/`obj` placement back, since those tests need it for some reason. Possibly doing that in this new project would make it work too.

However, since we don't really need to prove that Photino itself works in any particular way (we only need to show our libraries work when Photino is working), your workaround seems entirely fine to me as-is.
This change (and the stuff below) is due to updating to the latest Photino.
The old code doesn't work in Photino anymore (apparently it was never supposed to work).
